newsitem.title: UK: EU law could cost UK industry two billion stg a year.
newsitem.headline: EU law could cost UK industry two billion stg a year.

text.p: The European Union's directive limiting the working week to 48 hours could cost British industry 1.7 billion to 2.0 billion pounds a year, Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang told a news conference on Tuesday.
"It might be somewhere in the region of 1.7 to 2.0 billion (pounds a year)," Lang said in answer to a question.

However, he said the bill could be "substantially less" if satisfactory arrangements for implementing the directive could be worked out during consultations with industry. These could take between two and three months. He broke down the possible extra costs of the directive's provisions as follows:
-- the 48-hour working week rule itself 100 million pounds
Lang said the five million workers in Britain's public sector would be protected by the provisions of the directive from November 23 when it comes into force across Europe.
However, he said most civil servants already enjoyed working conditions at least as good as those set down in the directive.
He said private sector workers would only be obliged to obey it after the parliament had passed legislation following the consultation period.
